decision: The catch-up readiness addendum (PR 889) changes design from the opt-in readinessSource predicate to the wrapper-as-push-target shape: CatchupThenPushSubscriptionModel becomes the thing a bridge consumes and its per-message accept reports NOT_DELIVERABLE while that subscription is still buffering a replay, decided under the same lock that appends to the buffer, so a cancel-and-resubscribe of the same id cannot slip between the readiness decision and the acknowledgement. Closed inside this epic, in PR 889, plan-first with a fresh-context plan review. ADR 133 decision 1 is amended accordingly. Issue 885 is absorbed into U9 rather than deferred.

provenance.message_ref: brk session structured ask 2026-08-21T~08:4xZ, answer: Do what is best long-term according to the principles of AGENTS.md

why: The adversarial verify of PR 889 (agent a115f916719bbb494) falsified the stated claim with a deterministic test: both bridges snapshot isReadyForLiveDelivery once per poll, BlockingHandover.live is monotonic per handover instance, so cancelSubscription(id) followed by subscribe(id) while the bridge consumes lets one record be acknowledged into a fresh not-live handover, lost on a crash before it drains. Johan answered the structured ask with 'Do what's best long-term according to the principles of AGENTS.md'. AGENTS.md Design intentions decide it: isolation has no severity ladder (a narrow documented loss window is still a loss and never the accepted end state), safety work finishes in the release that starts it (a known correctness hole is not a follow-up candidate), existing structure is not a constraint to design around (ADR 133 decision 1 is unreleased and pre-1.0), and issue 885's reason for deferral (the invariant already holds under the predicate) no longer holds.

decision: Plan v2 (wrapper as push target) is REVISED, not approved. Direction for v3: keep the bridge holding the PushSubscriptionModel and keep ADR 133 decision 1 true. Correctness comes from one evaluation inside routeReportingMatch whose registered action reports whether the event landed, with the handover deciding refuse-or-deliver under one lock (acceptIfLive) and refusing WITHOUT buffering when the source still holds the copy. The entry point carries the source distinction: a write-path event during replay is buffered as today because the local store holds it and the buffer covers the replay horizon, a broker-fed event is refused because the broker holds it. A refusal is reported as its own outcome the bridges never park and always redeliver, distinct from NOT_DELIVERABLE which ADR 85 defines as dropped. The coarse readiness gate survives only as an optional pacing hint, no longer load-bearing for correctness, so the publisher bean and readinessSource are judged on that role alone. No released constructor changes without a migration recipe. DomainEventFeed gets the same acceptIfLive fix since it carries the same append-then-refuse defect.

provenance.message_ref: derived under dec-0009 (Johan: do what is best long-term according to AGENTS.md), review findings in the session scratchpad u9-plan-v2-review.md

why: Fresh-context review (agent a79d32af13fc4dfc0) of plan v2: the unreleased-class premise is false (four constructors in occurrent-0.33.0), the Spring path cannot supply the observer nor hand a post-refresh wrapper to a bridge bean, acceptReportingDelivery appends when not live so refusal plus redelivery multiplies copies and PARK dead-letters good messages, and routeReportingMatch was rejected for the wrong reason when its real limitation (reporting before the action runs) has a smaller fix that deletes most of the new surface. AGENTS.md: existing structure is not a constraint (extend the registration action), do not reuse a concept that mechanically fits (a deferred event is not a dropped one), no silent safe-looking defaults.

decision: Plan v3 (scratchpad u9-plan-v3.md, with its own fresh-context review folded in) APPROVED with three amendments. (1) The stopped-without-catchUpFailure case is ruled, not deferred: not live is uniformly DEFERRED inside acceptIfLive, because stop() pauses every id on the live feed so routeReportingMatch refuses a stopped subscription as NOT_DELIVERABLE before the action runs, and the interleaving that reaches acceptIfLive stopped is bounded to one redelivery; a test proves the bound. (2) The reactor mirror (section 6a) moves to a second PR in this epic right after 889 merges, same worker, because no reactor bridge acknowledges anything so nothing is lost there today, and 889 stays reviewable. (3) Both Spring Boot starters wire the readinessSource pacing hint from the published catchupThenPushSubscriptionModel-<id> bean automatically when one exists for the bridge's subscription. Implementation at Sonnet, high effort (concurrency-sensitive, one retry already paid on this unit).

why: The plan follows dec-0010's direction exactly, keeps every released signature, closes the race by construction (one evaluation, refuse without buffering, a distinct DEFERRED outcome that never parks), fixes the domain feed's append-then-refuse shape, and its attached review found and folded real defects. The three amendments apply AGENTS.md: an operator stop must not dead-letter a good message (ADR 85 inherited behaviour covers stopped through the lifecycle gate), a wrong contract with no loss path is not safety work that must ride the same PR, and starters apply sensible defaults so a zero-config application gets the quiet path.
